> A mini Keyboard with a few input buttons so that I can enjoy reading/watching even more! I aim to use several buttons and a rotary resistor so that I can change the volume. Using a USB connector between the mini keyboard and xiao, they will be able to communicate with one another.

### 2026-11-02: Today, I planned what sort of project I wanted to do this week.

**0.5h**

Today, I planned what sort of project I wanted to do this week.

I looked through the options and decided I wanted to re-attempt making a mini keyboard. The first time I attempted it was the first time I ever touched Kicad. Unfortunately, the guide utterly confused me and didn't explain things well enough in my opinion, so I decided to focus on other things at the time. However, with renewed courage and experience, I will fight to make this work this time.

I always wanted to make this mini keyboard, as I really like reading and watching on the internet, and so I use the arrow keys, etc, as shortcuts. Sometimes I clicked 0 on the keypad part of the keyboard when watching a video. If you know, you know my suffering. So having a mini keyboard with only things I want or need, that won't happen anymore. Sure I could just turn on num lock, but what about the volume? Pausing? Those are no where near the arrow keys.

Since I am free to do whatever I want this week, I wanted to solve a little problem of mine.

This is what I have so far -->

### 2026-11-04: Today, I continue  working on the schematic diagram.

**1.5h**

Today, I continue  working on the schematic diagram.

Earlier today, I found a arduino ide library specifically for what I wanted to do. It made it so that when a method was called with the specific key in its parameter, like "KEY_ UP-ARROW", the computer would actually get sent that key, which is pretty cool. I think for the volume, I'll just use they keyboard library to make it so that when the rotary encoder is turned left, it triggers F6 instead of coding for volume specifically, as that seems more universal as I would need to download a program that allows the chip to increase/decrease the volume.

The links -->
https://docs.arduino.cc/language-reference/en/functions/usb/Keyboard/

https://docs.arduino.cc/language-reference/en/functions/usb/Keyboard/keyboardModifiers/

I just realised, why am I using a raspberry pico pi? I'm practically wasting it with the small amount of pins I'll actually use. I think I'll switch to the Seeed xiao I have used in the earlier projects, plus its smaller.

### 2026-11-06: Today I will continue working on the rotary encoder code.

**2h**

Today I will continue working on the rotary encoder code.

So in simple words, the rotary encoder tells the chip which way it is turned by checking whether the A or B pin first contacts GND, making a complete circuit for a bit. I will continue using https://lastminuteengineers.com/rotary-encoder-arduino-tutorial/ to figure out how to do the code.

I'm trying to understand and explain how exactly the code works, as I don't want to just copy and paste. I want to learn -->

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/xLV9v2yZsf8cQU2Q5GZ9YV3OSKXKe8Gz/77e93c611cc02f9c3f7aae8975ef048d65ac4341e47a1aec68a409225fb392c4.png)
